comment: Per-kind section specification for wiki entity notes. This file decides which headings a generator owns; the paired template in references/templates decides what a note looks like. doctor checks the two agree. 'guidance' is sent to the drafting model verbatim, so it is prompt text as much as configuration. Length budgets are first guesses and expected to be retuned once real runs land.

concept.lead_guidance: One or two sentences defining the idea. Say what it claims, not why it matters. No hedging, no 'refers to'.

sections.guidance: The definition. One or two sentences.

sections.heading: Key Points
sections.guidance: Three to five bullets: the moves the concept makes, what it argues against, where it does work. One claim per bullet, no bullet repeating the lead.

sections.heading: Origin
sections.guidance: One line: who introduced it, in what work, and when. Omit entirely rather than guessing a date.

sections.heading: Key Thinkers
sections.guidance: Names only, optionally with a three-word gloss. People who developed or contested the concept, not everyone who cited it.

sections.heading: Distinctions
sections.guidance: Where the concept is routinely misread, and what it is confused with. Include only a confusion the sources actually flag.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic. Rendered from the archived sources, never written by the model.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored. Never written or read by the pipeline.
Deterministic. Rendered from the citations the draft actually used.

term.lead_guidance: One sentence that lets a reader use the term correctly. This is a glossary entry, not an essay.

sections.guidance: The definition, in one sentence. Expand an acronym on first use.

sections.heading: Usage
sections.guidance: One or two lines on where the term is used and by whom, including any field-specific narrowing of its meaning.

sections.heading: Origin
sections.guidance: One line: where the term comes from. Omit rather than guessing.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.

practice.lead_guidance: One or two sentences naming the practice and what doing it consists of.

sections.guidance: What the practice is and what performing it involves.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.guidance: Three to five bullets describing the method as a practitioner would recognize it. Describe the technique, do not instruct the reader.

sections.heading: Origin
sections.guidance: One line: the tradition or lineage it comes from, and roughly when.

sections.heading: Key Thinkers
sections.guidance: People who codified or transmitted the practice.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.

figure.lead_guidance: One or two sentences: field, dates in parentheses, and the one thing they are known for. This is the single most useful line on the card and it is what every figure note currently lacks.

sections.guidance: Who they are: nationality or field, lifespan in parentheses when the sources give it, and what they are known for. Never invent a date; omit the parenthetical instead. For a living person, claim nothing the archived sources do not state.

sections.heading: Key Ideas
sections.guidance: Three to five bullets, each naming one idea and saying what it claims. Wikilink a concept only when that note already exists.

sections.heading: Key Works
sections.guidance: Format each as *Title* (year). Two to five entries, the works they are actually read for. Omit a year you cannot source.

sections.heading: Position
sections.guidance: One or two lines: the tradition they work in and what they argue against. Omit unless the sources make it clear.

sections.heading: Associated Concepts
sections.guidance: Deterministic. Rendered from the note's own related property, never written by the model.

sections.heading: Colleague Thinkers
sections.guidance: Deterministic. Rendered from the note's own related property, never written by the model.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.

work.lead_guidance: One or two sentences: author, year, form, and the work's central claim or premise.

sections.guidance: Author, year, and form, then the one-line thesis or premise. Omit a year you cannot source.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.guidance: Three to five bullets tracing what the work does, in its own order. Works for an argument, a narrative, or a track list alike.

sections.heading: Key Concepts
sections.guidance: Ideas this work is the standard citation for. Wikilink a concept only when that note already exists.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.

place.lead_guidance: One or two sentences: what and where it is.

sections.guidance: What the place is and where. Name the containing region so the note is locatable without a map.

sections.heading: Significance
sections.guidance: Two to four bullets on why the place recurs as a subject — historical, cultural, or personal.

sections.heading: Context
sections.guidance: One line of orienting detail: region, period, scale.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.

event.lead_guidance: One or two sentences: what happened, when, and where.

sections.guidance: What happened, with the date and place. Omit a date you cannot source rather than approximating it.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.guidance: Three to five bullets in chronological order. Facts, not interpretation.

sections.heading: Significance
sections.guidance: One or two lines on what changed as a result.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.guidance: Deterministic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.guidance: Owner-authored.
Deterministic.
